variations.name: Electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement (acid extraction from seawater)
variations.description: Electrochemical cells split seawater into an alkaline stream that is returned to the ocean to absorb more atmospheric CO2 and an acidic stream managed separately, giving precise, mining-free control over how much carbon the sea draws down.

companies.name: Ebb Carbon
companies.what: Bipolar-membrane electrochemistry bolted onto desalination/industrial seawater outfalls to make alkalinity and split off acid; pursues co-located deals with desal plants.
companies.signal: ~$40M raised; 350,000-tonne 10-yr offtake with Microsoft (Oct 2024); Google offtake (Dec 2025); Saudi Water Authority MoU for up to 85 Mt/yr at full deployment.

companies.name: Equatic (UCLA spinout)
companies.what: Seawater electrolysis that co-produces solid carbonates plus green hydrogen, neutralizing the acid stream by mineralizing CO2; sells CDR + H2 bundles.
companies.signal: $11.6M Series A closed Aug 2025 (Temasek Trust C3H, Kibo); Equatic-1 demo plant in Tuas Singapore live Q1 2026 with PUB; Boeing pre-buy of 62,000 t + 2,100 t H2; ~$500/t.

companies.name: Captura
companies.what: Direct Ocean Capture via bipolar-membrane electrodialysis that strips gaseous CO2 out of seawater (rather than dosing alkalinity); see direct ocean capture variation — straddles both.
companies.signal: $45.3M Series A (Apr 2024, Eni/Equinor/Maersk/Aramco); Kona 1,000 t/yr pilot; Equinor validated for commercial 30,000-50,000 t/yr facility Nov 2025.

companies.name: Vycarb
companies.what: Brooklyn-based CO2 neutralization plus in-situ carbon sensing to make fully-measured, dose-controlled alkalinity additions at the waterline.
companies.signal: Founded 2022; early-stage; cited among credible US OAE developers but pre-large-offtake.

companies.name: Capture6
companies.what: Turns desalination waste brine into a solvent that mineralizes CO2 in one step while recovering >50% freshwater; electrochemically derived alkalinity loop (also in brine variation).
companies.signal: $27.5M Series A + project funding Mar 2025 (Hyundai ZER01NE, Energy Capital Ventures); Palmdale Water District (CA), plus WA Australia and South Korea projects.

variations.name: Mineral ocean alkalinity enhancement (lime/olivine/carbonate dosing at outfalls and from vessels)
variations.description: Finely ground alkaline minerals (magnesium hydroxide, hydrated lime, or processed limestone) are dosed into seawater at power-plant/wastewater outfalls so dissolved CO2 converts to stable bicarbonate, locking carbon away for millennia while countering ocean acidification.

companies.name: Planetary Technologies
companies.what: Doses magnesium hydroxide slurry into power-plant cooling-water and wastewater outfalls (Halifax, Norfolk VA) and verifies removals; the volume leader on credits delivered.
companies.signal: Delivered world's first independently verified OAE credits (625.6 t) to Stripe/Shopify/British Airways Jun 2025; $31.3M Frontier offtake (Aug 2025) for 115,211 t; ~$271/t; $11.3M Series A Oct 2024.

companies.name: Limenet
companies.what: Calcines limestone and reacts the resulting lime + recovered CO2 with seawater in a reactor to produce pH-neutral calcium bicarbonate dosed to the sea; world's largest OAE pilot plant.
companies.signal: Italian plant operational since Sept 2023, ~800 t CO2/yr scaling to 2,000 t/yr (2025) and 100,000 t/yr target by 2028; raised EUR 5M Sept 2024; first blockchain OAE credits via Carbonmark.

companies.name: CREW Carbon (formerly CarbonRun spinoffs / Yale)
companies.what: Adds alkalinity at municipal wastewater treatment plants to enhance carbon uptake in receiving waters; US East Coast deployments.
companies.signal: Early-stage; cited among credible US OAE developers (Vycarb, Vesta, CREW); pre-large-offtake.

variations.name: River and watershed liming (river alkalinity enhancement)
variations.description: Crushed limestone is dosed into acidified rivers via automated dosers, simultaneously repairing acid-rain damage and boosting the river's natural ability to pull CO2 from the air before the alkalinity reaches the sea.
variations.white_space: Nascent and effectively single-player: river liming is cheap and ecologically familiar (long used for fish habitat), so the physics are de-risked, but measurement/verification of incremental CO2 uptake in flowing freshwater is the hard part and the regulatory/credit category is brand new. An opening exists for credible MRV-first entrants in geographies with many acidified or neutral-pH rivers (Scandinavia, Appalachia, Canada).

companies.name: CarbonRun
companies.what: Canadian spinout (Dalhousie) running automated limestone dosers on rivers, pioneering 'river alkalinity enhancement' as a distinct CDR pathway with a credible sub-$100/t trajectory.
companies.signal: $25.4M Frontier offtake (Stripe, Shopify, McKinsey, Meta, Google) to remove 55,442 t 2025-2029; generated world's first river alkalinity enhancement credits; +$1M Stripe R&D grant.

variations.name: Coastal enhanced weathering (olivine sand placement)
variations.description: Olivine sand is placed in the nearshore where wave energy grinds and dissolves it, generating bicarbonate alkalinity that captures CO2 while doubling as shoreline-erosion protection — marine enhanced rock weathering powered by free wave action.
variations.white_space: Thin field with one clear lead. Slow, hard-to-measure dissolution kinetics in cold/low-energy water and trace-metal (nickel/chromium) permitting concerns deter entrants, and MRV is contested. Opening: integration with publicly funded coastal-resilience/beach-nourishment budgets (which dwarf carbon revenue) could subsidize deployment and de-risk the model.

companies.name: Vesta (Project Vesta)
companies.what: Integrates olivine 'carbon-removing sand' into coastal construction and beach-nourishment projects (Coastal Carbon Capture), harnessing wave energy for marine enhanced rock weathering.
companies.signal: Flagship pilot placed 7,000 cubic yards of olivine sand at Duck, North Carolina (Jul 2024); trials in Caribbean, Hawaii, India; pilot targets >=5,000 t CO2; backed by Stripe Climate, TreadRight.

variations.name: Direct ocean capture (seawater CO2 stripping via electrodialysis/vacuum)
variations.description: Rather than dosing alkalinity, these systems acidify a seawater stream (or apply vacuum) to convert dissolved bicarbonate into gaseous CO2 that bubbles out for permanent storage or reuse, then return the CO2-depleted water to re-absorb atmospheric carbon.

companies.name: Captura
companies.what: Caltech spinout using bipolar-membrane electrodialysis to split seawater and strip out pure CO2 gas; the most commercially advanced DOC player, targeting ~$100/t.
companies.signal: $45.3M Series A (Eni Next, Equinor, Maersk Growth, Aramco, National Grid, JAL); Port of LA (100 t/yr) + Kona Hawaii (1,000 t/yr) pilots; Equinor validated for 30,000-50,000 t/yr commercial plant (Nov 2025).

companies.name: SeaO2
companies.what: Amsterdam-based DOC using electrochemistry plus vacuum to shift the carbonate equilibrium and extract CO2 gas from North Sea water; proposes Europe's first standalone DOC field test.
companies.signal: Raised >EUR 2M (Nov 2024); pilot plant in Scheveningen Harbor targeting 250 t CO2/yr launched summer 2025; field-validated with real North Sea water 2025; BlueInvest-backed.

companies.name: Equinor (incumbent partner)
companies.what: Norwegian energy major running a joint technology-qualification program to validate and scale DOC for commercial offshore deployment, supplying engineering and offshore siting.
companies.signal: Completed DOC qualification with Captura Nov 2025; designing 30,000-50,000 t/yr facility with European/UK/APAC sites; also a Captura equity investor via Equinor Ventures.

variations.name: Brine-based capture and mineralization (desalination brine alkalinity loops)
variations.description: Desalination reject brine is intercepted and processed electrochemically to extract alkalinity or mineralize CO2 into solid carbonates, simultaneously solving desal's hypersaline-waste problem and recovering extra freshwater plus saleable chemical co-products.

companies.name: Capture6
companies.what: Converts desal waste brine into a CO2-mineralizing solvent in a single step while recovering >50% of freshwater; co-locates at water utilities to share economics across water + carbon.
companies.signal: $27.5M Series A + project funding Mar 2025 (Tetrad, Hyundai ZER01NE, Energy Capital Ventures); Palmdale Water District (CA) eliminating ~100 acres of brine ponds; projects in WA Australia, South Korea, NZ.

companies.name: Ebb Carbon
companies.what: Intercepts desalination brine discharge and runs it through an electrochemical system to produce ocean-bound alkalinity plus chemical co-products and higher freshwater yield.
companies.signal: ~$40M raised; desal-integration strategy anchored by Saudi Water Authority partnership (up to 85 Mt/yr potential at full deployment).

companies.name: IDE Technologies
companies.what: Global desalination EPC that patented a sustainable desalination process recovering calcium and CO2 from seawater to cut external chemical purchases and enable mineralization.
companies.signal: Established desalination incumbent (multi-decade, global plants); 'Desalination Brine Mining' commercialization program; representative example of incumbent brine-valorization.

variations.name: Macroalgae/sargassum cultivation and deep-ocean sinking
variations.description: Fast-growing seaweed (kelp or pelagic sargassum) is cultivated or collected, then sunk to the deep ocean (>1,000 m) so the fixed carbon is locked away for centuries — appealing because seaweed needs no land, fertilizer, or freshwater, though sinking permanence and MRV remain contested.
variations.white_space: High-churn, low-survivor variation. The economics are brutal: seaweed CDR credits are expensive and seaweed can't be readily monetized on existing carbon markets, and recent in-situ studies show sunk kelp degrades rapidly, undercutting permanence claims. Running Tide's collapse chilled buyers. Opening favors players that pair biomass with a saleable co-product (biomaterials, feed) so carbon is upside, not the whole business case.

companies.name: Running Tide
companies.what: Sank limestone-coated wood waste seeded with kelp ~200 miles off Iceland to >1,000 m, bundling biomass sinking with alkalinity; once the highest-profile seaweed-sinking venture.
companies.signal: Shut down June 2024 citing lack of voluntary-market demand; raised ~$50M (2017-2024); laid off remaining 32 staff (peak 120); generated controversial woodchip credits.

companies.name: Seafields
companies.what: Aims to farm pelagic sargassum in stationary open-ocean aquafarms off West Africa (using artificial upwelling for nutrients) and bale/sink it for durable storage.
companies.signal: ~$3.9M in grants/equity/debt by Mar 2025 plus a 2025 crowdfunding round (~$226K from 140+ investors); unveiled a $1B project concept; partners with MacroCarbon; pre-commercial.

companies.name: Carbonwave
companies.what: Upcycles Caribbean sargassum blooms into biomaterials (cosmetic emulsifier, fertilizer); a co-product-first model where carbon is secondary, hedging against thin CDR markets.
companies.signal: Raised $5M round bringing total to ~$12M; building large-scale emulsifier production in Puerto Rico.

companies.name: Kelp Blue
companies.what: Cultivates giant kelp in deep offshore waters (Namibia) for biostimulants and other products while studying blue-carbon sequestration; product-led rather than pure-sinking.
companies.signal: Operating offshore Namibia; partnering with Wageningen University and Algaia on the SeaSolv seaweed-processing project; pre-large-offtake on carbon.

variations.name: Terrestrial biomass sinking in anoxic basins
variations.description: Agricultural and forestry residues (woodchips, bagasse, corn stalks) that already captured CO2 on land are sunk into oxygen-free deep basins where decomposition is extremely slow, aiming to lock the carbon away for centuries to millennia.

companies.name: Rewind
companies.what: Israeli venture sinking woody/agricultural residue into the anoxic Black Sea seabed (2,300 m), arguing near-zero decomposition; the largest dedicated anoxic-basin biomass player.
companies.signal: Tested in Sea of Galilee, Germany, and off Trabzon Turkey; permitting with Romania for 100 t at 600 m; targets 1 Mt/yr by 2030 and 50 Mt long-term; Stripe/Activate R&D grant.

companies.name: Carboniferous
companies.what: Sinks sugarcane bagasse and other crop residue into the hypersaline, anoxic Orca Basin in the Gulf of Mexico (Anoxic Biological Carbon Sequestration); won rare US EPA research permit.
companies.signal: EPA MPRSA research permit (applied May 2025) to sink 20 sacks of sugarcane residue at 2,200 m; $250K Frontier R&D grant + $500K Stripe/Activate grant; faces Friends of the Earth opposition.

variations.name: Microalgae cultivation with terrestrial/desert storage
variations.description: High-growth microalgae are grown in open coastal ponds using seawater, then harvested, dried into hypersaline flakes, and buried on land in arid regions for ~1,000+ years — moving the storage step onshore to sidestep ocean-permanence and MRV uncertainty.
variations.white_space: Sparse, capital-intensive niche dominated by one credible scaler. It needs cheap flat coastal desert land plus seawater plus burial sites — a rare geographic combination — and competes with cheaper enhanced-weathering and DAC on cost. Opening: co-siting with desalination or solar in MENA/North Africa where all three inputs coincide, and where buried biomass MRV is simpler than ocean sinking.

companies.name: Brilliant Planet
companies.what: Grows engineered microalgae in open-air seawater ponds on coastal desert (Morocco), then dries and buries the biomass onshore as hypersaline flakes for ~1,000-year storage.
companies.signal: $12M Series A (Union Square Ventures, Toyota Ventures), >$25M total; 70,000 m2 demo site (~100 t/yr) targeted early 2025; sold 1,500 t to Block via Watershed; 270,000 t/yr commercial plant goal by 2030.

variations.name: Iron and nutrient ocean fertilization
variations.description: Adding trace iron (or other limiting nutrients) to iron-poor surface waters stimulates phytoplankton blooms that absorb CO2 and, when the plankton die, export carbon to the deep ocean as 'marine snow' — historically the most studied and most controversial marine CDR pathway.
variations.white_space: Almost no commercial players because the pathway is heavily stigmatized (London Protocol restrictions, the 2012 Haida rogue-dumping episode) and ecological side-effects plus verification of permanent export remain deeply uncertain. The serious activity is research consortia, not startups; the one venture that flirted with it (Gigablue) drew accusations of de-facto fertilization. An opening exists only behind rigorous, permitted, MRV-heavy science — and only if governance frameworks legitimize it.

companies.name: Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS)
companies.what: Non-commercial international research consortium (60+ scientists, 37 institutions) designing transparent, permitted iron-fertilization field experiments to resolve efficacy and ecosystem impacts.
companies.signal: Planning multi-region trials (off Alaska/Canada, Pacific upwelling zones, Southern Ocean) over a 5-10 yr horizon; estimated first-of-kind LCOC ~$200/t; research stage, not selling credits.

companies.name: Gigablue
companies.what: Israeli startup deploying patented particles meant to grow algae then sink rapidly to the seafloor; markets it as distinct from iron dumping though scientists dispute that.
companies.signal: Claimed sale of 200,000 carbon credits (2025) despite little public technical data; NZ EPA found a planned 1,000 t particle deployment amounted to illegal ocean dumping; credibility widely questioned.

variations.name: Artificial upwelling/downwelling
variations.description: Wave- or pump-driven systems bring cold, nutrient-rich deep water to the sunlit surface (upwelling) to trigger photosynthesis and carbon export — or push surface water down (downwelling) — aiming to enhance the ocean's natural biological carbon pump.
variations.white_space: Barely past the theoretical stage with only micro-scale tests; engineering durable wave-driven pumps in the open ocean is unproven at scale and modeled CDR efficiency is low (likely capping around ~100 Mt/yr, far below gigaton hopes), so few investors commit. Opening is narrow: ecosystem-restoration/fisheries co-benefits may fund early pumps where carbon alone cannot, but the carbon thesis itself is weak.

companies.name: The Sea Upwelling Company (formerly Ocean-Based Climate Solutions)
companies.what: Builds wave-powered open-ocean upwelling pumps that lift nutrients to the surface to trigger photosynthesis and food-web restoration alongside CO2 removal.
companies.signal: Deploying east of Bermuda with Bermuda Institute of Ocean Sciences — billed as the first open-ocean upwelling CDR project worldwide; early/demonstration scale.

companies.name: Sea-Up
companies.what: Designs, deploys, and operates wave-driven sea-upwelling pumps that deliver deep-water nutrients to the sunlit upper ocean to stimulate photosynthesis and restore sea life.
companies.signal: Early-stage developer building/operating pumps; pre-commercial, small-scale field activity.

companies.name: Seafields
companies.what: Uses artificial upwelling specifically to feed stationary sargassum aquafarms (overlaps the macroalgae variation) rather than for standalone bloom export.
companies.signal: ~$3.9M raised by Mar 2025 plus crowdfunding; partners with MacroCarbon on stationary aquafarms; pre-commercial.
